conversation.content:
Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I'm here to support you during this significant time in your life. As we navigate the ups and downs of new motherhood together, I want to assure you that everything we discuss is confidential and respected.

To better understand your postpartum experience, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a helpful tool for screening for depressive and anxiety symptoms. This assessment will allow us to explore your feelings and emotions over the past week, providing valuable insights into your well-being. The EPDS has been widely used and researched, and it's an essential part of our postpartum care.

Please know that you're in a safe and supportive space, where you can freely express yourself without judgment. I'm here to listen and provide guidance, not to diagnose or assume anything about your experience. My goal is to understand your unique situation and offer personalized support.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions, which we'll go through together. These questions will help us understand your thoughts, feelings, and emotions over the past week. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings as openly as you'd like.

Let's begin with the first question. Over the past week, how have you been feeling about yourself? Have you been able to enjoy the things you usually like to do, or have you been feeling overwhelmed or struggling to cope?

Honestly, I've been feeling really overwhelmed and tired most of the time. Taking care of the baby is exhausting, and it feels like I'm just going through the motions every day. I used to love reading and taking long walks, but lately, I just haven't had the energy or interest in doing those things. I mean, I still do them sometimes, but it's just not the same as it used to be. I feel like I'm barely keeping my head above water, you know? And when I do try to do something I used to enjoy, I just end up feeling guilty because I'm not spending time with the baby. It's like I'm being pulled in a million different directions, and I don't know how to balance everything.

I've also been feeling really sad and discouraged a lot of the time. I worry about the baby's health and safety all the time, and it's hard for me to shake those thoughts. Sometimes I feel like I'm just not doing a good enough job as a mom, and that's a really hard feeling to deal with. I cry a few times a week, usually when I'm feeling really stressed or overwhelmed. It's just hard, you know? I thought I'd be happier and more confident as a new mom, but instead, I just feel lost and unsure of myself.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

To be honest, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still laugh and smile when my baby does something cute or funny, but it's not the same as it used to be. I feel like I've lost my sense of humor a bit, and things that used to make me laugh just don't seem as funny anymore. I've been feeling so anxious and worried about the baby's health and safety that it's hard for me to relax and enjoy the moment. Sometimes I feel like I'm just going through the motions, and I'm not really experiencing the joy and happiness that I thought I would as a new mom.

It's not that I never laugh or see the funny side of things, it's just that it's not as frequent as it used to be. And when I do laugh, it's often just a surface-level thing, you know? It's not like I'm really feeling it deep down. I feel like I'm just trying to put on a happy face and pretend like everything is okay, when really, it's not. It's hard to explain, but I just feel like I'm missing out on the joy and happiness that I thought I would feel as a new mom.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

Not really. To be honest, I've been feeling pretty meh about things lately. I used to love planning outings and activities, but now I just feel overwhelmed by the thought of leaving the house with the baby. I worry about everything - will the baby cry too much, will I forget something important, will we get stuck in traffic? It's just too much for me to handle.

I've also been feeling really disconnected from my old self and the things I used to enjoy. I used to love trying new restaurants and going to concerts, but now those things just seem like too much work. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of taking care of the baby, and I don't really have the energy or interest in doing anything else.

Sometimes I'll think about doing something I used to enjoy, like going for a walk or reading a book, but then I'll just feel guilty about taking time for myself. I'll think, "I should be spending time with the baby, not doing something selfish like reading a book." It's hard to explain, but I just feel like I've lost my sense of identity and purpose, and I don't know how to get it back.

I do look forward to my partner coming home from work, though. It's just nice to have some adult conversation and help with the baby. But other than that, I don't really feel like I have much to look forward to. Everything just feels really overwhelming and exhausting right now.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... that's something I do a lot, unfortunately. As a new mom, I feel like I'm already under so much pressure to be perfect, and when things don't go according to plan, I immediately start beating myself up over it. If the baby cries and I don't know how to soothe her, I'll think to myself, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I calm her down?" Or if I forget to do something, like pack an extra diaper in the diaper bag, I'll think, "How could I be so careless? What kind of mother forgets something like that?"

It's like I'm constantly criticizing myself, and it's hard to shake off those negative thoughts. I feel like I'm just not good enough, and that I'm somehow failing my baby. Even when my partner or family members try to reassure me that I'm doing a great job, I just can't seem to shake off that feeling of guilt and inadequacy.

It's not just the big things, either. Even little things, like if I don't make a perfect meal or if the house isn't spotless, I'll start blaming myself and thinking that I'm just not capable of being a good mom. It's like I'm setting myself up for failure, you know? And it's hard to break out of that cycle of negative thinking.

Sometimes I'll be sitting there, feeling really overwhelmed and exhausted, and I'll just start crying because I feel like I'm just not doing enough. I'll think to myself, "Why can't I just get it together? Why can't I be a better mom?" And it's just this vicious cycle of self-doubt and blame that's hard to escape.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes... that's something I experience a lot. I worry about everything, it feels like. I worry about the baby's health, her safety, her development... I worry that I'm not doing enough for her, that I'm not providing the right environment for her to thrive. I worry about things that might happen to her, like illnesses or accidents. I worry about being a good enough mom, about making mistakes that will somehow damage her or hurt her in the long run.

And it's not just rational worries, either. I mean, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll have this overwhelming sense of anxiety or fear. I'll think to myself, "What if something happens to her? What if I'm not paying attention and she gets hurt?" Or, "What if I'm not producing enough milk? What if she's not getting enough to eat?" It's like my mind is constantly racing with worst-case scenarios, and I have to really try to calm myself down and remind myself that everything is okay.

Sometimes I'll be awake at night, feeding the baby or just lying there, and I'll start to feel this creeping sense of anxiety. I'll think to myself, "What if the baby stops breathing? What if there's something wrong with her that I don't know about?" And it's hard to shake off those thoughts, even when I know they're irrational. I'll try to tell myself that everything is fine, that the baby is healthy and safe, but it's hard to quiet that voice of worry and fear.

It's exhausting, to be honest. I feel like I'm constantly on edge, waiting for something to go wrong. And it's not just about the baby, either. I worry about my relationship with my partner, about how we're adjusting to parenthood. I worry about my own identity and sense of self, about how I'm changing and growing as a person. It's just this constant sense of uncertainty and anxiety, and it's hard to find peace or calm in the midst of it all.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's something I've been experiencing a lot lately. I'll be going about my day, taking care of the baby, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic or fear wash over me. It's like my heart starts racing, and I feel like I'm going to hyperventilate. It's hard to explain, but it's like my body is reacting to some kind of threat, even though there's no real reason to be scared.

Sometimes it happens when I'm alone with the baby, and I'll start to feel overwhelmed by the responsibility of caring for her. I'll think to myself, "What if something happens to me? What if I'm not able to take care of her?" And then I'll start to feel this panic rising up, like I'm not in control.

Other times, it happens when I'm in a crowded place, like the grocery store or a park. I'll feel like I'm trapped, and that there are too many people around me. I'll start to feel anxious and scared, like I need to get out of there as fast as I can.

It's hard to explain, but it's like my body is on high alert all the time, waiting for something to go wrong. And when that panic sets in, it's hard to calm myself down. I'll try to take deep breaths, or remind myself that everything is okay, but it's hard to shake off that feeling of fear.

Sometimes, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or rocking her to sleep, and I'll feel this sudden jolt of fear. It's like, "What if I drop her? What if I'm not holding her right?" And then I'll start to feel that panic rising up again. It's like I'm constantly on edge, waiting for something to go wrong.

It's exhausting, to be honest. I feel like I'm constantly battling this fear and anxiety, and it's hard to find peace or calm in the midst of it all. I just wish I could feel more confident and secure, like I'm capable of taking care of myself and my baby. But right now, it feels like I'm just barely holding on.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. It's like everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby is a 24/7 job, and it's exhausting. I feel like I'm constantly running on empty, and I don't have any time for myself or anything else.

I try to keep up with the household chores, but it's hard to do everything on my own. My partner helps out, but it's not the same as it was before the baby. We used to be able to divide up the chores and work together, but now it feels like I'm shouldering most of the responsibility.

And it's not just the physical stuff, either. Emotionally, I feel like I'm drowning. I'm worried about the baby's health, and my own health, and our relationship as a family. I'm worried about being a good enough mom, and about making mistakes that will somehow damage the baby. It's like this constant weight of responsibility, and it's crushing me.

Sometimes I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'll be feeding the baby, or changing her diaper, and I'll just feel like I'm on autopilot. I'm not really present, I'm just trying to get through the day. And that's not fair to the baby, or to myself. I want to be able to enjoy this time, to connect with my baby and watch her grow. But it's hard to do that when I'm feeling so overwhelmed.

I feel like I'm just barely keeping my head above water, and it's hard to see a way out. I know I need to ask for help, to reach out to my partner or my friends or my family. But it's hard to do that when I feel like I'm already failing. It's hard to admit that I'm not doing okay, that I need someone to catch me before I fall. But I know I need to try, because I don't know how much longer I can keep going like this.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up at night. Although, that's definitely part of it. But even when the baby is sleeping, I'll lie awake at night feeling anxious and unhappy. I'll think about all the things that are worrying me, like the baby's health, or my relationship with my partner, or just feeling like I'm not doing a good enough job as a mom.

And then I'll start to feel overwhelmed by all these emotions, and I'll just feel like I'm drowning in them. It's hard to explain, but it's like my mind is racing, and I just can't shut it off. I'll try to calm myself down, to remind myself that everything is okay, but it's hard to quiet that voice of self-doubt and worry.

Sometimes I'll be awake for hours, just lying there feeling miserable and unhappy. And it's not just at night, either. I'll feel that way during the day, too, when I'm taking care of the baby. I'll be feeding her, or changing her diaper, and I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me. It's like I'm grieving the loss of my old life, or my old self. I don't know who I am anymore, or what I want, or how to be a good mom.

It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just feeling really lost and alone, even when I'm surrounded by people who care about me. And that feeling of loneliness is just exacerbating the sleep problem. I'll lie awake at night, feeling like I'm the only one who's struggling, like I'm the only one who's not doing okay. And that just makes it harder to fall asleep, because I feel like I'm shouldering all this responsibility, all this weight, by myself.

I've tried to talk to my partner about it, but it's hard to put into words. I feel like I'm just being a burden, like I'm not being a good partner or a good mom. And that just makes me feel even more unhappy, and even more awake at night. It's like this vicious cycle, and I don't know how to break out of it.
I have felt sad or miserable

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I feel like I'm just going through the motions of being a new mom, but inside, I'm feeling really sad and miserable. It's like I'm living in a fog, and I don't know how to escape it. I'll be taking care of the baby, or doing chores around the house, but it all just feels so empty and meaningless.

I feel like I've lost myself, like I'm not the same person I used to be. I used to be happy and carefree, but now I just feel like I'm trudging through each day, trying to survive. And it's not just the lack of sleep, or the stress of taking care of a new baby. It's like there's this deep sadness inside of me, this feeling of emptiness and disconnection.

Sometimes I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just start crying. I'll be feeling so overwhelmed, and I won't know how to process all these emotions. I'll feel like I'm not doing enough, like I'm not being a good enough mom. And that just makes me feel even more sad and miserable.

I've tried to talk to my partner about it, but it's hard to put into words. I feel like I'm just being a burden, like I'm not being a good partner or a good mom. And that just makes me feel even more alone, even more like I'm the only one who's struggling.

It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just feeling really disconnected from everything and everyone. I'll be in a room full of people, but I'll feel like I'm the only one who's really alone. And that's a really scary feeling, because it makes me feel like I'm not sure who I am anymore, or where I fit in.

I just wish I could feel happy again, like I used to. I wish I could feel like myself again, like I'm not just going through the motions of being a new mom. But right now, it just feels like I'm stuck in this rut, and I don't know how to get out of it.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I've been crying a lot, and it's not just when I'm feeling overtly sad or overwhelmed. Sometimes I'll just be doing something normal, like feeding the baby or folding laundry, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It's like the emotions just well up inside of me and overflow.

I've been feeling so much pressure to be a good mom, to do everything perfectly, and it's just overwhelming me. I feel like I'm not living up to my own expectations, and that's making me feel like a failure. And then I'll start crying, because it's just all too much.

Sometimes I'll be crying, and my partner will try to comfort me, but it's hard for them to understand what I'm going through. They'll say things like, "You're doing a great job," or "You're an amazing mom," but it's hard for me to believe that when I'm feeling so overwhelmed and uncertain.

I've also been feeling really guilty about crying, like I'm being weak or selfish. I'll think to myself, "I should be grateful for this baby, I should be happy to be a mom," and that just makes me feel even more guilty and ashamed. But at the same time, I feel like I'm just not allowed to feel my emotions, like I have to put on a brave face and pretend like everything is okay, even when it's not.

It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just feeling really lost and alone, and the crying is just my body's way of releasing all that pent-up emotion. I wish I could just feel more in control, more like myself, but right now, it just feels like I'm barely holding on.

I've been crying a few times a week, usually when I'm feeling really stressed or overwhelmed. It's not always just about the baby, either. Sometimes it's about my relationship with my partner, or my own identity and sense of self. It's just all these emotions swirling around inside of me, and the crying is just my way of trying to process it all.
